text: Up twenty-nine in the NBA Finals. And the Spurs lost — by one.
Every shot gets graded. Distance, defender, angle — that's expected field goal percentage.
First half, the Spurs kept beating those odds. From the field: expected forty-nine, scored seventy.
Then the bill came. After the break: nineteen points on shots worth thirty-nine.
Mike Brown's answer: go small. Towns at center, four guys spaced around him.
That pulls Wembanyama away from the rim. One screen, one switch —
and the league's best rim protector is guarding Brunson twenty-seven feet out. Bang.
At the other end: four of nineteen in the fourth, with a defender's hand two and a half feet from the ball.
Spurs up one. Thirteen seconds left.
The shot clock is longer than the game, and the Knicks are in the penalty. Hold the ball, and they have to foul you.
Instead, Fox goes. A coin-flip layup nobody needed.
Five point seven left. The Spurs use their foul to give. Brown answers with five shooters.
Fox and Wemby both jump Brunson. Nobody touches Anunoby.
The Knicks led this game for fifty-three point eight seconds. It was enough.
